metadata.description:
Mincing garlic can be a tough time. But breaking it down to a paste? Probably...not any easier.

Watch as 50 people try to make garlic paste by any means necessary, including peeling, cutting, mincing, smashing and squashing.

summary.brief: A rapid‑cut montage shows many people each making garlic paste by peeling, crushing, and mincing garlic with a range of tools.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a graphic that reads “Epicurious – 50 People Try to Make Garlic Paste” while a garlic clove drops onto a wooden cutting board. The screen then splits into dozens of side‑by‑side panels showing a diverse group of participants—men, women, and a professional chef—working at wooden boards. Each person demonstrates a different step of making garlic paste: some peel whole bulbs by hand or with a small knife, others smash or press cloves with garlic presses, mortars and pestles, hand‑crank grinders, or blenders. Several participants chop peeled cloves with kitchen knives, holding the cloves steady with the opposite hand, and many sprinkle salt to help break the flesh down. A chef in a white jacket later appears, repeatedly chopping garlic and sprinkling salt while bowls of the mixture sit nearby. Throughout the three‑minute sequence the cuts are fast, there is no audible dialogue, and the visual focus remains on the hands, tools, and the evolving garlic paste. The montage ends with an Epicurious logo overlay.

action.detailed: Peel the garlic skins, then crush, grind, or chop the cloves with knives, presses, mortars, or other tools, adding salt as needed, until a smooth paste forms.
action.actor: Various participants, including a chef
